newsitem.title: USA: US Plains feedlot cattle not established - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains feedlot cattle not established - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Monday were not established, with packers not expected to replenish live inventory supplies until midweek following last week's active trading, feedlot sources said.

Light packer bids at $64.00 per cwt were passed by cattle owners asking $67.00-$68.00, with a few at $66.00, they said. Sales last week were brisk at $65.00, which was down $1.00 from the previous week.
Prices were expected to be supported this week by ideas packers were short bought on live supplies and needed cattle soon to fill beef orders, the feedlot sources said.
Feedlot cattle prices also were expected to be underpinned by bullish enthusiasm over USDA's monthly cattle report on Friday, the sources said.
The report showed December placements on large feedlots in the seven major cattle states at 98.0 percent of a year ago, which was well below average pre-report estimates of 108.2.

This week's showlist was pegged near 79,700 head, up 4,000 from last week in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma panhandle and close to 78,000 in Kansas, down 5,500. The Nebraska showlist was estimated near 83,000 head, down 1,000.
